question: Section 8's 'In short' says 'the series a model uses most are not the ones that make it more accurate'. At group level the realized moments are the trees' largest exogenous attribution and their second-largest removal (+1.6 / +1.8%). Replace it with the D18 result (the six groups beyond HAR + RM + FOMC hold 20-23% of the trees' attribution but give 4-11% of the gain)?

solvers.answer: Replace the clause, which is false at group and series level, with the D18 contrast on exogenous attribution (the six groups hold 45.2-48.0% of it; the full set's gain over HAR + RM + FOMC is 4-11% of its gain over HAR) plus the FOMC half (3.3-4.9% of exogenous attribution, 65-68% of the gain).

Retire the sentence and state the D18 result plainly from the C5 macros on the exogenous denominator: the six other groups hold 45.2-48.0% of the trees' exogenous attribution and deliver 4-11% of their gain; change the section opening (08:133-135) with it.

Replace the sentence, but not with the D18 contrast: in LightGBM and XGBoost the realized moments and the six groups have the same attribution share and the same removal cost, a substitutes pattern, so the contrast does not show attribution misleads. Use an FOMC-only sentence from existing macros.

refutation.note: All three lenses agree the sentence goes (false: the realized moments are the trees' largest exogenous group and second-largest removal; the top 10 series by the trees' own attribution keep \rhldEBLgbmBarRTen = 97% and \rhldEBXgbBarRTen = 96% of the every-bar gain). The majority replacement (evidence, author record: the D18 contrast) does not survive. Checked: (1) Decisive point, the twin rows, recomputed from scores_fomcfix/metrics.csv: removal cost as a share of the full set's gain over HAR is 9.6% (LightGBM) and 10.3% (XGBoost) for the realized moments, and 9.6% and 10.5% for the six groups together (HAR + RM + FOMC against the full set); their exogenous attribution is 47.0/50.0% (\rhfrcLgbmRmShareAll, \rhfrcXgbRmShareAll) against 48.0/45.2% (\rhfrcLgbmBeyondShareExogAll, \rhfrcXgbBeyondShareExogAll). By the D18 sentence's own yardstick the realized moments, which the same 'In short' says carry the ordinary days, would also be 'used but add little'. The contrast comes from the order of the decomposition (D18 accounts for RM first) and from substitution, which the 'In short' already states ('whose information the constituents' moments and the liquidity measures largely repeat'). tab:rh_fi_reconcile, which C5 puts in the same subsection, prints the two rows one above the other. (2) Added alone, liquidity, EW and VW each give 19.7-23.7% of the boosted trees' gain, as the realized moments do (21.2/23.4%); attribution does not overstate the six against what they add alone, and the author-record wording 'deliver 4-11% of their gain over the HAR benchmark set' misstates a gain beyond the base as the six groups' whole gain. (3) The 4% low end is the forest, whose remainder is not significant (\rhabRfFullVsAddRmFomcAllP = 0.096). (4) The \rhfrc macros are committed (c910c6b) but not input by the paper (grep), and C5's insertion waits on Q8 (Q-2026-10-29-09, T3 open); the FOMC sentence uses only loaded \rhfip and \rhab macros. (5) Author record: no author-typed message after 29 Oct 14:32 PDT (transcript bd4224e0 to 15:10 PDT, queued ones included) or log line decides this sentence; the coordinator's 14:37 PDT chat line calling the D18 contrast 'the clean use is not accuracy result' is agent text, unanswered. The attribution statement the author endorsed (claim 3, 27 Oct 22:52-22:53 PDT) is the FOMC one. (6) The referee's optional symmetric sentence needs two new generator macros, a reviewer's new number held as a proposal (report section 8.6), so it is not applied. (7) Voice: the referee's lead 'Attribution is a poor guide to the calendar's part:' is a verdict without a predicate (V4) before a colon; the final wording is the plain declarative (V1).

final_answer: Yes, replace the sentence, but with the FOMC fact rather than the D18 contrast, because the realized moments show the same attribution share and the same removal cost as the six groups in LightGBM and XGBoost (a substitutes pattern the 'In short' already states). In writeup/rehaul/08_feature_importance.tex, replace 'Attribution is a poor guide to all of this: the series a model uses most are not the ones that' (end of line 364) and 'make it more accurate.' (line 369) with exactly: The trees attribute \rhfipFomcBucketMin--\rhfipFomcBucketMax\% of their forecasts to the FOMC calendar, yet added alone to the HAR benchmark set it delivers \rhabTreeFomcGainShareMin--\rhabTreeFomcGainShareMax\% of their every-bar gain. Keep the 3c6ccc4 comment block (lines 365-368) intact and park the old sentence verbatim in a dated comment ('% 2026-10-29 (Q-2026-10-29-27, inferred T2). Was: ...'). Every macro is already loaded; no generator, macro or table change. The section opening (08:132-135) changes under Q-2026-10-29-26, not here.
answer_short: Sec. 8 'In short': 'the series a model uses most are not the ones that make it more accurate' becomes the FOMC fact (1.4-2.3% of the trees' attribution, 65-68% of their gain).
rationale: The sentence must go; all three lenses agree. The replacement the majority chose, the D18 contrast, has right numbers but cannot carry the claim it replaces: the realized moments show the same share and the same removal cost, so the contrast reflects the decomposition order and substitution, not misleading attribution, and a referee would read that off the reconciliation table printed beside it. The refutation succeeded, so the final answer is the referee's FOMC sentence, worded to V1/V4 and using loaded macros: T2 at best. Confidence 0.68: the FOMC claim is the one the author endorsed on 27 Oct, but D18 is his own question and two lenses expected him to want the six groups named in the summary.
